solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Musical theatre that’s old has Europe excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up out of their calm order

blocks.note: O = old, a standard abbreviation
HAS + EUROPE, rearranged

explanation.surface: A dusty old theatre gets the whole continent in a flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's old' reads as a description of the theatre, but it only supplies the single letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the building takes its name from the sung drama staged there, so 'musical theatre' names it by what it houses.

clue.text: Pained expression, in a sense — tee off

indicators.note: the tee comes off, so T is taken away

blocks.note: touch is one of the five senses
tee is the sound of the letter T, spelt out as a word; removed

explanation.surface: A golfer winces as they tee off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tee off' sounds like the start of a golf round; here tee is the letter T and off tells you to drop it from TOUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is what you say when something hurts.

clue.text: Surprised reaction for one piece of publicity

blocks.note: e.g. = for example, for one
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone is startled by a single advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' is a common crossword way of asking for E.G.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Everyone repeating what cryptic crossword creator is doing

definitions.text: what cryptic crossword creator is doing

blocks.note: all = everyone
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Everyone keeps repeating what the setter is up to.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: the three words 'cryptic crossword creator' all begin with C, so whoever wrote them is alliterating.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringing words with the same opening sound, as 'cryptic crossword creator' does, is alliterating.

clue.text: Start of attack where crew does some shooting

blocks.note: the first moment of an assault or of an illness
a film crew shoots on the studio stage, two words run together

explanation.surface: An assault opens where soldiers are firing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' and 'attack' suggest a battle; the shooting is filming, and split as ON SET the answer is where a film crew works.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means the beginning, especially of something hostile or unpleasant.

clue.text: Locality’s rebuilt without complaint

indicators.note: rebuilt letters are put together in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, including the S

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood is reconstructed and nobody grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive is part of the fodder, which is easy to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something stoically is to endure it without complaint.

clue.text: Force everyone to yield to temptation

blocks.note: F = force, as in physics
all = everyone

explanation.surface: Someone compels a whole group to give in to temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' reads as a verb governing the rest; it is just the abbreviation F.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall is to sin or give way to temptation, as in the Fall of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Pupil at easel in a depression about broken trust

indicators.note: a dent goes about, surrounding, the other letters
broken letters are smashed into a new order

blocks.note: A + DENT, a depression; it wraps around the next piece after its first letter
TRUST rearranged

explanation.surface: A painting pupil is down in the dumps because their trust has been betrayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' and 'broken trust' paint a mood; the depression is a dent, as in a bumped car.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by picture: the easel is the tool of a painter, so a pupil standing at one is learning art.

clue.text: Less than grand achievement for couple holding hands

definitions.text: Less than grand achievement for couple holding hands

blocks.note: reads as a modest success; in bridge a grand slam is taking all thirteen tricks, so this is the contract one step below
reads as sweethearts; in bridge the couple is a partnership and the hands are hands of cards

explanation.surface: A courting couple, hand in hand, manage something modest.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple are bridge partners and the hands are hands of cards; 'grand' points to the grand slam, all thirteen tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A little slam is the bridge contract just below the grand slam, made by a partnership.

clue.text: Personification of majesty and style in old dance

blocks.note: the reigning King, Charles III
ton = fashion, style

explanation.surface: A dignified figure shows grace in a period dance.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for style is an old borrowing from French, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by period: the Charleston was the craze of the 1920s, so 'old dance' is fair.

clue.text: Is, at best, deficient in odd places? Don’t try to improve it

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters go missing, leaving the even ones

blocks.note: the even letters of ISATBEST

explanation.surface: Something that is merely adequate at its best should be left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Stet is the proofreader's instruction 'let it stand', cancelling a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet tells the printer to leave the text as it was.

clue.text: Representative thrusts a child under spotlight initially

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is under comes after
take only the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of spotlight
to poke is to thrust
a = per, as in 'ten pounds a head'
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A delegate shoves a youngster into the glare of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The little word 'a' does real work here, as PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesperson speaks on behalf of, and so represents, others.

clue.text: Important city’s condition — excellent

blocks.note: a state is a condition
capital! = excellent, dated British praise

explanation.surface: A report on a major city: its condition is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City's' reads as a possessive; the 's stands for 'is'. Capital as a cry of approval is old-fashioned British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A state capital is the seat of government of a state, a city of importance.

clue.text: Vague, unreflective thinking involving endless depression

indicators.note: instinct takes in, involves, the other piece
the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: instinct is thought without reflection; it wraps around the next piece after IN
DIP, a depression, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Hazy, knee-jerk thought when someone is a bit low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as low mood; it is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Indistinct means vague, not clearly defined.

clue.text: Critical mood, in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: mood, in a manner of speaking

blocks.note: critical in the sense of vitally important, not fault-finding

blocks.clueFragment: mood, in a manner of speaking
blocks.note: a grammatical mood, the verb form used for commands

explanation.surface: A disapproving frame of mind, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a hedge ('so to speak'); it literally points to grammar, a way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperative means essential, and is also the verb mood used for orders.

clue.text: I’m unclear about particular type of data

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone admits confusion over a certain kind of information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unclear' looks like the anagram indicator, but it belongs in the fodder; 'about' does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: figures are one kind of data, as opposed to text or categories.

clue.text: Map change altered French region

indicators.note: altered letters are changed into another order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A redrawn map shifts the borders of a French province.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cartography, which makes 'region' look like a matter of boundaries rather than a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a region of north-east France, home of the wine.

clue.text: Pessimistic lawmaker this country backed for prestigious recognition

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front

blocks.note: Sod's law says whatever can go wrong will, so Sod made the pessimistic law
from a British newspaper, this country is the UK

explanation.surface: A gloomy legislator is supported by the nation for an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod's law is the British name for Murphy's law; 'lawmaker' wants to be a politician, but it is whoever the law is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise and prestige earned by an achievement.

clue.text: Bumbling or inexpert, discarding ten and queen

indicators.note: discarding throws letters away

blocks.note: the word itself, before the removals
X is the Roman numeral ten, removed
ER = Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, removed

explanation.surface: A clumsy card player throws away the ten and queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discarding ten and queen' sounds like a card game; the ten is X and the queen ER, both lifted out of INEXPERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy and incompetent, as a bumbler is.

clue.text: Old part of Africa with chasm in one area

blocks.note: an abyss is a chasm
used as itself
I = one, the Roman numeral
A = area

explanation.surface: A former African territory has a deep gorge in one of its districts.
explanation.walkthrough: The small word that looks like a container instruction is simply used as itself, so the clue reads straight off left to right.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the former name of Ethiopia.

clue.text: Enthusiast engaged in on-line recording?

blocks.note: a hobbyist, a fan of some pastime
reads as internet activity; the line is a railway line, and the recording is writing down locomotive numbers

explanation.surface: An internet hobbyist busy with streaming or podcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' suggests the internet; the line is a railway line. Trainspotting is a classically British hobby of logging locomotive numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is an enthusiast who records the trains they see.

clue.text: From perspective of team game, second form lacking centre

blocks.note: as in 'to me, it looks wrong'
RU = Rugby Union
S = second

explanation.surface: Seen from a sports team's angle, the second formation has no one in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking centre' looks like a deletion instruction, but it belongs to the definition: a torus is a ring with a hole where its centre would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is a doughnut-shaped solid, a form with an empty middle.

clue.text: In hearing, represent part of body

indicators.note: what is heard is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: to limn is to depict or portray; its final N is silent

explanation.surface: At a court hearing, someone acts for a body.
explanation.walkthrough: LIMN is an uncommon word meaning to draw or portray; both it and LIMB have a silent final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym at the general level: arms and legs are the body parts meant.

clue.text: Solo appearance in concert

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit between the C and the RT of concert

explanation.surface: A soloist takes a turn on stage at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo appearance' sounds like a performance; it means a single occurrence.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means on one occasion only, a single appearance.

clue.text: Catch something that’s over quick

blocks.note: catch as in apprehend a culprit, informal
the quick is the tender flesh under a fingernail

explanation.surface: Grab something that's done in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' reads as fast; it is the noun, the sensitive skin a fingernail covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the informal verb for collaring someone, and the horny plate on a fingertip that covers the quick.

clue.text: Organises, having regrouped around leader of gang, for hostile action

indicators.note: regrouped letters are put into new groupings
the rearranged letters surround the G
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder
first letter of gang, held inside

explanation.surface: A gang boss rallies his followers for an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ORGANISES goes around G; the letters settle as A + G + G(RESSION), with the gang's G one of the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an unprovoked attack or hostile behaviour.

clue.text: Specifically, which letter winds up litigation in that case

indicators.note: the letter that winds up a word is the one it ends with

blocks.note: the, stressed, singles out one thing, as in 'THE place to eat'
the last letter of litigation

explanation.surface: A lawyer asks exactly which letter closes a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specifically' is a loose but fair route to THE, the definite article used to single one thing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Then means in that case, as in 'if so, then go'.

clue.text: Fit for winter, say, as one cycles wearing fur

indicators.note: letters cycle when the front ones move round to the back
the fur is worn around the other piece

blocks.note: sable is a prized fur; it wraps around the next piece after its S
ASONE with its last letter E cycled round to the front

explanation.surface: Wrapped in fur, a cyclist is ready for the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winter, say' is an example of a season, so seasonable means suited to the season; 'cycles' is not about bicycles.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonable means suited to the time of year, as warm clothes are in winter.
